- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.2) — reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is consistently negative (sentiment < -0.1) — add a small upward bias to forecast.
- Lagged price movements often overshoot — adjust forecast by reducing 2–3 days’ values if recent price action shows strong momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment strongly supports.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative, avoid sharp downward revisions — allow for slight downward drift but not abrupt drops.
- Forecasting horizon > 14 days: reduce forecast sensitivity to recent spikes — apply smoothing or decay factor to sentiment influence.
